<body>
  <header>
    <div class="brand">
      <h1>Decision science — the questions this system is built to answer</h1>
      <p>Causal effect, uncertainty, explore versus exploit, off-policy evaluation, constrained economics, and a loop that learns from its own prices</p>
    </div>
  </header>
  <div class="layout">
    <nav class="toc" id="toc"></nav>
    <article>

<section class="card" id="different">
  <p class="phase">Why this role is different</p>
  <h2>Why this is different</h2>
  <p>Most machine learning systems learn from a dataset that was collected by someone else. A ranking model sees clicks that happened under yesterday’s ranking. A demand forecast sees orders that happened under yesterday’s prices. The model is a spectator. This system is not. When it chooses a 10% discount for Maya on SKU-1234, that choice changes whether she buys, what margin lands, and which row appears in tomorrow’s training file. The decisions made by the model influence the data the model sees next.</p>
  <p>That is the job. You are not fitting a score that a human will later interpret. You are intervening in a commercial process, measuring what the intervention caused, and feeding that measurement back so the next intervention is better. The long-term bet in this repository is to build that loop once — ingest, guardrail, score, choose, log propensity, join outcomes, evaluate a challenger, promote only if it wins — and then apply it across channels, SKUs, and eventually a portfolio of businesses. Selecting the right method matters more than pledging a particular library. The S-learner in <code>stage4_causal.py</code> is a stand-in you can swap for EconML; Thompson sampling in <code>stage5_bandit.py</code> is a stand-in you can swap for a LinTS posterior. The contract around them stays: a legal action set, a logged propensity, a join on <code>decision_id</code>, and a gate that can refuse to ship.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="because">
  <p class="phase">The first question</p>
  <h2>What happens because we change a price</h2>
  <p>A naive dashboard answers a different question: what happened next. After we discounted, conversion went up. That is association. Shoppers who were going to buy anyway may have been the ones who received the discount, or a campaign may have run in the same week, or inventory may have been healthier on the discounted SKU. The question this system is built to answer is causal: what would have happened to purchase, margin, and retention if we had shown a different price to the same shopper in the same context.</p>
  <p>Stage 4 does not predict “will they buy.” It predicts expected reward as a function of context and action, μ(x, a). The lab S-learner in <code>stage4_causal.py</code> takes the feature vector from preprocess — segment, price sensitivity, churn risk, LTV, cold start — and each surviving discount arm, and returns a mean and a standard deviation. Reward is not hardcoded to conversion. <code>versions.yaml</code> can pin margin, revenue, LTV, or a composite, because the economic object we care about is not always a click.</p>
  <p>To keep that estimate honest, some traffic never sees the bandit. The gateway can assign a <code>holdout</code> variant; the orchestrator then forces list price. Holdout is not wasted traffic. It is the clean comparison that lets you keep estimating causal effects after the bandit has taken over the rest of the store. Offline, <code>backfill.py</code> reconstructs features as of the decision timestamp rather than “whatever is in the profile now,” because training on the future is how you invent effects that were never caused by the price.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="uncertainty">
  <p class="phase">The second question</p>
  <h2>How uncertainty should affect a decision</h2>
  <p>A point estimate is not a decision. If two arms have similar μ but one has been seen a thousand times and the other is a deep discount on a cold-start guest, treating them as equal is how you overfit last week’s luck. The S-learner already widens σ for deeper discounts, for customers flagged cold-start, and when sensitivity sits far from the prior. The bandit then samples from that posterior, not from the mean. High σ makes an arm more likely to win a Thompson draw, which is how uncertainty buys information. Low σ makes the greedy arm dominate, which is how certainty harvests margin.</p>
  <p>Uncertainty also changes what you are allowed to do when the machinery is sick. If the causal model times out, stage 4 reuses last scores or a uniform prior and marks the call degraded. If Event Hubs cannot take the log, exploration stops, because an unlogged experiment is not an experiment — it is a price change you cannot evaluate. If App Configuration cannot be read, the system fails closed to list price. Uncertainty about the world is a reason to explore. Uncertainty about whether you can even record the experiment is a reason to stop.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="explore">
  <p class="phase">The third question</p>
  <h2>When to exploit what we know versus experiment to learn</h2>
  <p>Stage 5 is contextual Thompson sampling with an explicit explore floor. Most calls draw a score for each legal arm from a Gaussian around μ and σ and pick the winner. A fraction of calls, set by <code>PDS_</code> epsilon (5% in the lab), pick uniformly so the logging policy cannot collapse onto one arm. Every twentieth live call is forced to explore for the same reason. A request with <code>mode: exploit</code> skips that floor and takes the highest μ — that is checkout when you have already decided not to learn, or a campaign that must not randomize.</p>
  <p>The choice is not “always explore” versus “always greedy.” It is sequential. Stickiness in the control plane remembers an offer for the same shopper and SKU so you do not re-randomize inside a session. Frequency caps in guardrails stop you from “learning” by discounting the same person twice a week. When logging is incomplete, the policy switches to exploit so the data you do have remains usable for off-policy evaluation. Active learning here is not a separate service. It is the bandit’s decision, under constraints, about which price is worth showing in order to know more.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="challenger">
  <p class="phase">The fourth question</p>
  <h2>Can we estimate a challenger before fully deploying it</h2>
  <p>Yes, and you must, because shipping a new policy to 100% of checkout to “see if it works” is an expensive experiment you cannot undo on the orders already taken. Off-policy evaluation in <code>offline/ope.py</code> scores a candidate policy on historical logs: inverse propensity (IPS), its stabilized cousin SNIPS, a direct method that uses the causal model, and doubly robust (DR), which mixes them so a bad propensity or a bad μ does not take the whole estimate with it. A bootstrap interval and an effective sample size tell you whether the number is a measurement or a rumor. Rows without a propensity, or marked excluded from training, never enter that calculation.</p>
  <p>The gate in <code>offline/gate.py</code> is the adult in the room. A challenger is allowed near traffic only if DR says it beats the current policy, the lower end of the interval still beats current, ESS is healthy, fairness and latency checks pass. If they pass, the registry marks Production and a rollout ladder begins at shadow — the new revision logs, it does not serve — then 1%, 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%. If they fail, the current champion stays. That is how you estimate the value of a challenger policy before fully deploying it, and how you refuse to confuse a better offline notebook with a better business.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="constraints">
  <p class="phase">The fifth question</p>
  <h2>Optimize economics while respecting constraints</h2>
  <p>Unconstrained “optimal price” is a fiction. Stage 2 removes arms before the model is allowed to want them. A price below cost plus minimum margin is gone (vendor and finance). A price below MAP is gone (vendor agreement). A discount on a SKU that is not discountable is gone. Stock under the safety threshold blocks discount so you do not learn by emptying a warehouse. A shopper who has already used the frequency cap is not discounted again (customer and brand). Missing consent means generic treatment, not a personalized cut. A bot score high enough to be a scraper does not get exploration. A competitor bound keeps you from wandering so far that operations cannot explain the shelf. A VIP fairness rule stops the model from quietly giving one protected-looking segment a systematically deeper cut. List price is always left on the ladder so the system can fail closed.</p>
  <p>The control plane adds constraints that change without a new model: kill switch and merchandiser freeze force list price on the next request; a daily discount budget increments until the cap, then the bandit is not allowed to spend more. Stickiness is a customer constraint of a different kind — we already made a promise. Constrained optimization in this repo is not a separate solver. It is “optimize μ only over the legal set,” which is the form that survives contact with a real catalog.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="hte">
  <p class="phase">What you will do</p>
  <h2>Causal and heterogeneous treatment-effect modeling</h2>
  <p>A treatment effect that is the same for every shopper is rarely the one you want to ship. VIP, at-risk, returning, new, and guest do not share a conversion curve. The S-learner conditions on x: sensitivity raises the lift of a discount, churn risk punishes it, LTV weights retention into the reward, segment shifts the baseline. That is heterogeneous treatment effect modeling in the small. The same stage boundary is where a DR-learner, a causal forest, or an EconML estimator would sit later. You pick the method that the data and the decision can support. You do not start there if a calibrated linear μ already ranks arms well inside the guardrails.</p>
  <p>Heterogeneity that you cannot identify from consented features is not a feature you add by sneaking in protected attributes. Fairness evaluation in <code>offline/fairness.py</code> looks at segment price gaps after the fact. Audit attributes, if they exist, stay out of the vector that stage 4 sees. The modeling job includes knowing what must not enter x.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="calibration">
  <p class="phase">What you will do</p>
  <h2>Uncertainty estimation and calibration</h2>
  <p>Thompson sampling is only as honest as the σ you feed it. The lab grows σ with discount depth and cold start; a production LinTS backend would use the usual quadratic form in the posterior covariance. Propensity is the other calibration. For two arms it is a Gaussian tail; for more it is a Monte Carlo share of Thompson wins, floored at 0.05 so IPS never divides by zero. If every σ is zero, propensity collapses to 1 on the greedy arm — a warning that you have stopped being able to evaluate alternatives.</p>
  <p>OPE diagnostics are how you find out the logging policy and the candidate have drifted too far to share a support. Effective sample size is the number of historical decisions that still count under the new policy’s weights. If ESS is tiny, you do not have a counterfactual estimate. You have a story. Calibration work in this role is making sure μ, σ, propensity, and ESS describe the same world the shopper was in.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="sequential">
  <p class="phase">What you will do</p>
  <h2>Contextual bandits, active learning, sequential decisions</h2>
  <p>Checkout is not a batch. Each request arrives with a context, an action set that guardrails already shrunk, and a history encoded in features and in the sticky map. Contextual Thompson sampling is the sequential policy. Epsilon and the forced explore tick are the active-learning budget. Stickiness is how you avoid treating two page views as two independent experiments. Campaigns in <code>decide_batch()</code> are sequential decisions at list scale: still logged with propensity, still frequency-capped, never an email of a price that is not already in the offer ledger.</p>
  <p>Reinforcement learning in the long-horizon sense — a policy that plans over a customer lifetime — is a later method, not a starting requirement. The sequential object you have to get right first is the one-step contextual bandit with a logged propensity and a reward that can be redefined toward LTV when the data can support it. Judgment is noticing when the horizon has grown enough that one-step μ is no longer the right method, and not a day earlier.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="policy">
  <p class="phase">What you will do</p>
  <h2>Policy learning and constrained optimization</h2>
  <p>A policy here is not a notebook that ranks SKUs. It is a function from context to a distribution over legal arms, version-pinned in <code>versions.yaml</code>, served by the orchestrator, and named so OPE can say “this policy” versus “that one.” Learning a better policy means training a new causal model and a new bandit posterior on joined, point-in-time rows, then asking the gate whether the new function is allowed to take traffic. Constrained optimization is upstream of that function: the feasible set is the output of guardrails plus control-plane flags. You do not learn a policy that violates MAP and then clip it. You never score the illegal arm.</p>
  <p>The reward definition is a policy choice as much as the sampler is. Optimizing conversion will spend margin; optimizing margin will refuse discounts a growth team wanted; a composite is an explicit trade. Changing the reward is how you apply the same loop to a different commercial objective without pretending the math was objective all along.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="counterfactual">
  <p class="phase">What you will do</p>
  <h2>Counterfactual and off-policy evaluation</h2>
  <p>Every live decision writes an experience tuple in <code>stage7_logging.py</code>: context hash, candidate arms, chosen arm, propensity, policy id, causal model id, candidate-set version, variant, sticky replay, exclude-from-training. That tuple is the difference between a bandit you can evaluate and a random number generator with a dashboard. Outcomes join later on <code>decision_id</code>, not on customer_id, with a seven-day window net of refunds. Joining on the person mixes people. Joining on the decision asks what that intervention caused.</p>
  <p>IPS reweights history by π_new / π_old. SNIPS stabilizes the weights. DR adds the causal model’s guess and corrects it with the residual, so you are not betting the company on one estimator. Overlap between the logging ladder and the candidate ladder is measured because OPE is undefined when the new policy puts mass on arms the old policy never showed. If the hub is down, you buffer and stop exploring — otherwise the propensities you log are fiction and every later counterfactual number is too.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="champion">
  <p class="phase">What you will do</p>
  <h2>Experimentation and champion / challenger</h2>
  <p>The champion is the current policy pin. A challenger is a new causal artifact plus a new bandit, sitting in the registry until the gate speaks. Holdout traffic is the experiment that never uses the bandit, so you can still talk about causal lift against list price after years of personalization. Shadow is the experiment that runs the challenger without showing it. Canary is the experiment that shows it to 1% with App Insights watching p99, 5xx, logging completeness, reward versus predicted μ, propensity PSI, and segment price gaps. Rollback is one traffic-weight command, not a war room hope.</p>
  <p>The gateway assigns <code>holdout</code>, <code>bandit</code>, <code>shadow</code>, or <code>treatment</code>. Bots do not get exploration; they would poison the very data the challenger needs. Success of a challenger is not a higher OPE point estimate in isolation. It is that estimate, a healthy ESS, a fairness gap inside tolerance, a holdout that still exists, and a canary that did not have to be pulled.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="production">
  <p class="phase">What you will do</p>
  <h2>Production ML infrastructure, monitoring, automated deployment</h2>
  <p>The online path is FastAPI with a p99 budget under 100 ms. Version pins ride on every request so a score is attributable to a model. Hot reload in stage 10 swaps pins without a rebuild. Kill switch and freeze live in the control plane so legal and merchandising do not wait for a data scientist. Metrics sit on arm distribution, exploration rate, propensity, guardrail blocks, and stage timings. Fallbacks are a ladder: Redis down still prices, Cosmos down uses a warm catalog, causal timeout uses last scores, log failure stops explore, config failure fails closed.</p>
  <p>Automated deployment is tests, an image, a new Container Apps revision, and a gate that can refuse. Azure is the production shape of the same adapters: Redis for features, Cosmos for catalog and offers, Event Hubs for the experience tuple, ADLS and Azure ML for the night shift, App Insights for the canary. You do not rewrite causal or bandit to “be Azure.” You change <code>services/</code>. Production ML in this role is making the loop run when a real channel is calling, and making it stop when the log, the fairness gap, or the latency says so.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="success">
  <p class="phase">The bar</p>
  <h2>What success looks like</h2>
  <p>Success is not a better offline metric. A prettier DR number that never faces holdout, or a model that wins OPE because ESS collapsed onto a handful of VIPs, is not the job. The systems you build should produce measurable economic lift in controlled experiments — holdout versus bandit, champion versus canary — in units of margin, revenue, or LTV that finance would recognize. They should generalize across businesses in the sense that the loop is the same: legal action set, logged propensity, join on the decision, gate, shadow, ramp. They should learn from their own interventions, which is why an unlogged explore is forbidden and why backfill is point-in-time. They should safely automate an increasing share of real commercial decisions: more SKUs, more channels, more of the day without a merchandiser in the loop, and a kill switch that still works at 2 a.m.</p>
  <p>Over time the goal is simple. The system should become better at operating the business because it has operated the business. That sentence is the reward function for the role, and it is why this repository logs what it did.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="looking">
  <p class="phase">Judgment, not a checklist</p>
  <h2>Skills this system actually uses</h2>
  <p>Exceptional technical ability here looks like knowing which method the decision can support today. Machine learning and statistical modeling show up as the S-learner, the Thompson posterior, and the bootstrap around OPE. Causal inference and experimentation show up as holdout, μ(x, a) rather than “what happened next,” and a refusal to train on future features. Recommendation and marketplace judgment show up as a discrete arm ladder, frequency caps, and stickiness instead of an unconstrained continuous price. Bandits, optimization, and active learning show up as stage 5 plus the epsilon floor plus the legal set from stage 2. Uncertainty estimation shows up as σ and propensity. Counterfactual evaluation shows up as IPS, SNIPS, and DR. Production ML shows up as FastAPI, pins, metrics, fallbacks, and the Azure adapters. Python is the language of the loop; SQL and large behavioral datasets are what the lake becomes when bronze is no longer JSONL on a laptop.</p>
  <p>Matching a framework checklist is the failure mode. Shipping LinTS because the paper is fashionable, when overlap is already too thin for OPE, is how you automate a worse business. The strong candidate uses this lab to show they can pick the S-learner, then say out loud what evidence would justify replacing it.</p>
</section>

<section class="card" id="loop">
  <p class="phase">The long-term opportunity</p>
  <h2>The continuous loop</h2>
  <p>Build the capability once. Apply it across a portfolio of decisions. The objects change — price, coupon, rank, credit limit, send-or-not — the loop does not.</p>
  <div class="diagram">context x, legal arms A(x)
        │
        ▼
  score μ(x,a), σ(x,a)          causal / HTE
        │
        ▼
  sample / ε-explore            contextual bandit
        │
        ▼
  show price (intervention)
        │
        ▼
  log (x, a, π, versions)       experience tuple
        │
        ▼
  outcome y | decision_id       purchase, refund, return
        │
        ▼
  join + point-in-time x        lake / backfill
        │
        ▼
  train, OPE, fairness, drift
        │
        ▼
  gate → shadow → canary → champ
        │
        ▼
  better decision on the next request</div>
  <p>Open the Online PDS tab and run a price for Maya. Then run holdout on the same SKU and notice only list price remains. Then open Offline learning and run OPE. That path — not a slide — is the job: decision, intervention, outcome, learning, better decision.</p>
</section>

    </article>
  </div>

# Personalized Pricing on Azure — deploy script (Phase 1–4)
# Run from the Pricing repo root in PowerShell:
#   pwsh -File infra/azure-up.ps1
# Requires: Azure CLI, Docker Desktop, logged-in az account.

param(
    [string]$Location = "canadacentral",
    [string]$EnvName = "dev",
    [string]$Prefix = "pds"
)

$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
$suffix = Get-Random -Minimum 1000 -Maximum 9999
$rg = "rg-$Prefix-$Location-$EnvName"
$acr = ($Prefix + "acr" + $EnvName + $suffix).ToLower()
$envNameAca = "cae-$Prefix-$EnvName"
$appName = "ca-$Prefix-api"
$workspace = "log-$Prefix-$EnvName"
$kv = "kv-$Prefix-$EnvName-$suffix"
$appcs = "appcs-$Prefix-$EnvName-$suffix"

Write-Host "Container app  : $appName"
Write-Host "Key Vault      : $kv"

az acr create --resource-group $rg --name $acr --sku Basic --admin-enabled true | Out-Null
az acr login --name $acr

docker build -t "$acr.azurecr.io/pds-api:v0.1.0" .
docker push "$acr.azurecr.io/pds-api:v0.1.0"

az monitor log-analytics workspace create --resource-group $rg --workspace-name $workspace --location $Location | Out-Null
$workspaceId = az monitor log-analytics workspace show --resource-group $rg --workspace-name $workspace --query customerId -o tsv
$workspaceKey = az monitor log-analytics workspace get-shared-keys --resource-group $rg --workspace-name $workspace --query primarySharedKey -o tsv

az containerapp env create `
    --name $envNameAca `
    --resource-group $rg `
    --location $Location `
    --logs-workspace-id $workspaceId `
    --logs-workspace-key $workspaceKey | Out-Null

az keyvault create --name $kv --resource-group $rg --location $Location | Out-Null
az appconfig create --name $appcs --resource-group $rg --location $Location --sku Free | Out-Null

az containerapp create `
    --name $appName `
    --resource-group $rg `
    --environment $envNameAca `
    --image "$acr.azurecr.io/pds-api:v0.1.0" `
    --registry-server "$acr.azurecr.io" `
    --target-port 8080 `
    --ingress external `
    --cpu 0.5 --memory 1Gi `
    --min-replicas 1 --max-replicas 3 `
    --env-vars "PDS_ENV=azure-$EnvName" "PDS_HOST=0.0.0.0" "PDS_PORT=8080" `
    --query properties.configuration.ingress.fqdn -o tsv

Write-Host ""
Write-Host "Done. Open https://<fqdn>/  (printed above)"
Write-Host "Save these names: rg=$rg acr=$acr kv=$kv appcs=$appcs"

===== FILE: README.md =====
# Pricing Decision Service

Online pricing pipeline that turns a checkout request into a **guardrailed, logged, explorable price**.

The service follows the stage contract in the spec: ingest → preprocess → guardrails → candidates → causal scores → Thompson sampling → post-process → async log → client response, with a fallback ladder that always returns a price.

## Pipeline

| Stage | Module | Budget (p99) |
|---|---|---|
| 0 Ingestion | `stages/stage0_ingestion.py` | 2ms |
| 1 Preprocess | `stages/stage1_preprocess.py` | 15ms |
| 2 Guardrails | `stages/stage2_guardrails.py` | 5ms |
| 3 Candidates | `stages/stage3_candidates.py` | 2ms |
| 4 Causal scoring | `stages/stage4_causal.py` | 30ms |
| 5 Bandit | `stages/stage5_bandit.py` | 10ms |
| 6 Post-process | `stages/stage6_postprocess.py` | 3ms |
| 7 Logging | `stages/stage7_logging.py` | async |
| 8 Response | `stages/stage8_response.py` | 2ms |
| 9 Fallback | `stages/stage9_fallback.py` | — |
| 10 Cache / hot reload | `stages/stage10_cache.py` | — |

**Default reward:** expected margin `(price − cost) × P(purchase)` via an S-learner. **Default policy:** contextual Thompson sampling with a 5% ε floor and a propensity floor of 0.05 (so IPS/DR never divide by zero).

Client responses never include propensity, model IDs, or scores. Those live only in the experience log (`data/log_buffer/decisions.jsonl`) for OPE and audit.

## Quick start

```bash
cd Pricing
python -m venv .venv
.venv\Scripts\activate          # Windows
pip install -e ".[dev]"
pytest
```

One-shot decision from the example request:

```bash
python -m pricing_decision.cli decide -f examples/request.json --explain
```

HTTP API:

```bash
python -m pricing_decision.cli serve
# POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/price
# POST http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/price:explain   (internal)
# GET  http://127.0.0.1:8080/health
```

Example request:

```json
{
  "customer_id": "c_91823",
  "session_id": "s_abc",
  "sku": "SKU-1234",
  "cart_value": 50.0,
  "channel": "web",
  "device": "mobile",
  "geo": "CA-ON",
  "ts": "2026-09-11T14:22:01Z"
}
```

Example client response:

```json
{
  "price": 44.99,
  "currency": "USD",
  "discount_pct": 10,
  "badge": "10% off",
  "coupon_code": "SAVE10-...",
  "reason_codes": ["segment:returning", "policy:ts_v7", "arm:disc_10"],
  "decision_id": "...",
  "expires_at": "2026-09-11T14:32:01Z"
}
```

## Demo catalog

| ID | Role |
|---|---|
| `c_91823` / `SKU-1234` | Happy path, returning customer |
| `c_vip` / `SKU-VIP` | VIP — narrower ladder, no badge |
| `c_risk` | At-risk — deeper discounts if guardrails allow |
| `c_noconsent` | Personalization off → list price |
| `SKU-LOW` | Low stock → discounts blocked |
| `SKU-LOCKED` | Not discountable → list price |

Missing `customer_id` is treated as **guest**. Unknown SKU returns **404**.

## Config

Pinned versions and rules live in `configs/`:

- `versions.yaml` — `policy_id`, `causal_model_id`, `guardrail_version`
- `guardrails.yaml` — margin floor, MAP, frequency cap, inventory, fairness
- `ladders.yaml` — per-segment discount arms
- `features.yaml` — defaults, TTLs, clip bounds, train-time means/stds
- `catalog.yaml` — SKUs and customer feature snapshots

In-flight requests keep the version pins attached at ingestion, so a hot reload (`POST /v1/admin/reload`) cannot change a decision mid-flight.

## Fallback ladder

1. Full pipeline  
2. Cached causal scores on model timeout  
3. Segment defaults if the feature store is down  
4. ε-greedy if the bandit errors  
5. List price if every discount arm is blocked  
6. Static catalog price if everything else fails  

Degraded decisions are flagged `exclude_from_training=true` so they do not bias OPE.

## Production swaps

| Local stand-in | Production |
|---|---|
| In-memory feature store | Redis online store |
| JSON guardrail rules | Config service / Rego |
| S-learner prior | ONNX / registry model (`dr_v3`, Dragonnet, …) |
| JSONL buffer | Kafka `pricing.decisions.v1` + schema registry |
| In-process metrics | Prometheus + OpenTelemetry spans |

The stage interfaces stay the same; only the service adapters change.

from pathlib import Path

import yaml

raw = yaml.safe_load(Path("configs/azure_components.yaml").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
groups = {g["id"]: g for g in raw["groups"]}
by: dict[str, list] = {}
for c in raw["components"]:
    by.setdefault(c["group"], []).append(c)
badge = {"must": "Must have", "should": "Should have", "later": "Later / do not start here"}
out: list[str] = []
out.append('<section class="card" id="components">')
out.append('  <p class="phase">Bill of materials</p>')
out.append("  <h2>All Azure components for this project</h2>")
out.append(
    '  <p class="lead">This is the shopping list. <b>Must have</b> is required for a working pricing loop. '
    "<b>Should have</b> is required before public traffic. <b>Later</b> means do not start there. "
    "Put every data resource in Canada Central.</p>"
)
out.append(
    '  <div class="callout">Build in this order: foundation → hosting → config → Redis/Cosmos → '
    "Event Hubs/ADLS → Azure ML → Front Door/APIM → private network. Change code only in <code>services/</code>.</div>"
)
for gid, g in groups.items():
    items = by.get(gid, [])
    if not items:
        continue
    out.append(f"  <h3>{g['title']}</h3>")
    out.append(f'  <p class="lead">{g["about"]}</p>')
    for c in items:
        out.append('  <div class="box" style="margin:10px 0">')
        out.append(
            f'    <h4>{c["name"]} <span class="chip">{badge.get(c["required"], c["required"])}</span> '

        )
        out.append(f'    <div class="tool">{c["tool"]} · replaces: {c["replaces"]}</div>')
        out.append(f'    <p><b>Why:</b> {c["purpose"]}</p>')
        out.append(f'    <p><b>Dev SKU:</b> {c["sku_dev"]} · <b>Prod SKU:</b> {c["sku_prod"]}</p>')
        out.append(f'    <p><b>How:</b> {c["how"]}</p>')
        out.append(f'    <p><b>Watch out:</b> {c["pitfall"]}</p>')
        out.append("  </div>")
out.append(
    '  <label class="step"><input type="checkbox" data-k="all-components" />'
    "<span>I know week-1 must-haves versus week-8 edge/network, and I will not start on AKS or Service Bus.</span></label>"
)
out.append("</section>")
Path("_components_snip.html").write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
print("ok", len(raw["components"]))


===== FILE: scripts/_prose_components.py =====
from pathlib import Path

SECTION = r'''<section class="card" id="components">
  <p class="phase">Bill of materials</p>
  <h2>All Azure components for this project</h2>
  <p>You do not provision this list on day one. You grow it in the same order the system itself depends on: a place to run, then a way to change rules and hide secrets, then the two stores on the hot path, then a log that never lies about propensity, then overnight training, and only then a public door. Every database, cache, and log that holds shopper or decision data is created in Canada Central. When you connect these services, you change adapters under <code>services/</code>. You do not rewrite the causal model or the bandit.</p>
  <h3>Foundation</h3>
  <p>Start with a dedicated development subscription and the Entra directory that comes with it. That subscription is the billing and permission root; production pricing data should never live in a personal account. Sign in with <code>az login</code> and confirm you have Contributor. People use Entra to open the portal and the CLI; the Container App later uses a managed identity in the same directory so GitHub never holds a long-lived client secret. Create one resource group in Canada Central and put everything for this environment inside it, because deleting that group is how you stop paying. On the same day, set a Cost Management budget that emails you at a modest cap. A budget warns; it does not always shut resources off. Finally create a single Log Analytics workspace for the environment. Container Apps, App Insights, and later APIM should all write there. Several workspaces make simple questions impossible to ask.</p>
  <h3>Hosting</h3>
  <p>Azure Container Registry is the private shelf for Docker images of this app. Names are globally unique. Basic SKU is enough in development; production can move to Standard or Premium and, later, a replica in Canada East. A Container Apps environment is the cluster those images join, and you attach Log Analytics when you create it. The Container App itself is this FastAPI process: stages 0 through 10, a small CPU and memory footprint at first, replicas when traffic grows, and revisions so a new policy can take one percent of calls without replacing the old one. In development ingress can be external so you can open a browser; in production it should be internal behind API Management, and <code>/v1/price:explain</code>, <code>/v1/control</code>, and admin reload must never be on the public product. A Container Apps Job is the same codebase on a schedule for campaign lists. Do not fire thousands of single HTTP calls from Logic Apps with no backpressure. Do not begin on AKS or App Service. Container Apps is the host until you have a platform team and a scale problem that revisions cannot solve.</p>
  <h3>Config and secrets</h3>
  <p>Give the Container App a system-assigned managed identity and grant that identity roles, rather than baking Cosmos or Redis keys into environment variables. Key Vault holds the remaining secrets: Redis URL, Event Hubs send string, App Insights connection string, Cosmos key until you switch the SDK to Entra. Use RBAC on the vault, not a mix of access policies. App Configuration is the live rulebook that used to be <code>control_plane.yaml</code> and <code>versions.yaml</code>: kill switch, merchandiser freeze, policy and model pins, daily discount budget. Those flags must refresh in seconds. If App Configuration cannot be read, fail closed to list price using a cache no older than a minute. Free SKU is fine in development; production wants Standard and a replica in Canada East.</p>
  <h3>Online data plane</h3>
  <p>Two stores sit on the request. Redis, on TLS port 6380, is the millisecond cache that replaces the in-memory feature store and sticky-price map. Keys are short-lived: features, a sticky offer for shopper and SKU, frequency caps, and an incremented discount budget. If Redis is unavailable you still return a price from coarser defaults, because checkout cannot wait. Basic C0 is enough to learn the adapter; production should be Premium, zone redundant, and private. Cosmos DB is the system of record that replaces <code>catalog.yaml</code>, identity profiles, the coupon list, and decision lookup. Use separate containers partitioned on sku, customer_id, offer code, and customer_id again for decisions. Serverless is the right development SKU. Production should autoscale, back up, and fail over to Canada East. A coupon in Cosmos is a promise: a later policy change must not void a code already shown.</p>
  <h3>Streaming and lakehouse</h3>
  <p>Decision logs are telemetry, not a command queue, which is why Event Hubs with Kafka enabled replaces the JSONL buffer and Service Bus does not. One hub, <code>pricing.decisions.v1</code>, receives every <code>decide()</code> with propensity, policy id, candidate-set version, and experiment variant. Another, <code>pricing.outcomes.v1</code>, receives purchase, refund, and return keyed by <code>decision_id</code>, joined later on a seven-day window net of refunds. Joining only on customer_id will mix people and ruin OPE. Schema Registry versions that JSON so a silent field drop cannot poison training. ADLS Gen2 with hierarchical namespace is the lake: bronze for raw capture, silver for joined point-in-time rows, gold for OPE and campaigns. A plain blob account without HNS will fight Spark. Event Hubs Capture writes bronze on a timer so you do not need a custom consumer on day one. Keep capture in the same region. If the hub is down, buffer locally and stop exploring until it returns, or the propensities you log will be fiction.</p>
  <h3>Machine learning</h3>
  <p>Training never runs inside the online Container App. Azure ML is the workspace that replaces <code>data/registry/models.json</code> and laptop jobs: you submit causal, bandit, and OPE work, keep lineage, and register a model only when OPE beats the current policy and fairness and drift are acceptable. Serverless compute is enough for the numpy learners in this repo. A GPU cluster is a later choice and a common way to leave money running overnight. When joins no longer fit a single node, Microsoft Fabric or Azure Databricks in Canada Central reads the same ADLS paths that <code>offline/join.py</code> and <code>backfill.py</code> use today. The standing risk is training on “current” features instead of the values as of the decision timestamp.</p>
  <h3>Public edge</h3>
  <p>Skip Front Door and API Management until a real channel is calling you. Then Front Door Premium is the anycast door with TLS, bot manager, origin health, and a Canada POP. Point it at APIM or the app, never at the explain endpoint. Put the WAF in Detection for a week, then Prevention, with an allowlist for partner IPs. API Management is the product split that used to live in <code>gateway.py</code>: public price, checkout outcomes, CS lookup, and an internal product for explain and control. Developer SKU has no SLA; production should be Standard v2 or Premium on a VNet.</p>
  <h3>Observability and rollback</h3>
  <p>A bandit you cannot measure is just random prices. Application Insights, created against the same Log Analytics workspace, replaces in-process counters for production: duration of <code>/v1/price</code>, calls out to Redis and Cosmos, exceptions. Do not log propensity or PII in custom events; <code>decision_id</code> is enough on the public path. Metric alerts and an action group with a named owner fire on slow p99, 5xx, a gap between requests and Event Hub ingress, a stale kill switch, or a fairness gap. A workbook later fills the role of the lab Monitor tab: reward versus predicted value, propensity PSI, segment price gaps, logging completeness. Sampled telemetry makes those charts lie.</p>
  <h3>Security and Canada</h3>
  <p>In production, Redis, Cosmos, Key Vault, Storage, and Event Hubs should not have public endpoints. A VNet, private endpoints, and Container Apps integration are required, and DNS must be in place or the app will hang on names. Purview scans ADLS, classifies PII, and is how you show PIPEDA evidence that bronze decisions are not a free-for-all. Protected attributes used for audit must never enter the feature vector. Defender for Cloud watches for a public Cosmos account, Redis without TLS, and vulnerable images in ACR. Do not ship an image the registry has already flagged.</p>
  <h3>CI/CD</h3>
  <p>GitHub Actions with Entra OIDC is how a commit becomes a revision: tests, image, push to ACR, Container Apps update. Failed pytest must not deploy. Do not put <code>AZURE_CLIENT_SECRET</code> in GitHub. Federate the app registration and use <code>azure/login</code> with the federated token.</p>
  <h3>What to leave alone</h3>
  <p>AKS is a later host if Container Apps and a platform team cannot meet a sustained ten thousand decisions a second with a mesh you truly need. App Service slots are not a substitute for a propensity-logged canary. Service Bus is fine for occasional commands, not for this telemetry. Azure Communication Services is optional if you have no email provider; even then, never send a price that is not already in the offer ledger.</p>
  <label class="step"><input type="checkbox" data-k="all-components" /><span>I have read this as a sequence, not a shopping cart, and I will not start on AKS or Service Bus.</span></label>
</section>
'''

html_path = Path("docs/azure-implementation.html")

end = html.find('<section class="card" id="picture">')
if start < 0 or end < 0:
    raise SystemExit(f"markers missing {start} {end}")
html_path.write_text(html[:start] + SECTION.strip() + "\n\n" + html[end:], encoding="utf-8")
print("ok")

  <h2>1. What this project becomes on Azure</h2>
  <p>Every local piece has one production home. Keep this picture in mind while you build; it is the target, not a catalog of extras. A shopper on web, app, email, a till, or a partner never talks to Python. The call arrives at Front Door, which terminates TLS, picks a Canada POP, and should absorb bots so the bandit does not waste exploration on scrapers.   <div class="diagram">Channels (Web / App / Email / POS / Partners)
        │
        ▼

   ├─ Key Vault                 secrets, Event Hub conn, Redis key

        ▼

        │
        ▼
Container Apps revision split   shadow → 1% → 5% → 25% → 100%</div>
  <p>uvicorn on port 8080 becomes a Container App, and only later AKS if you outgrow revisions at something like ten thousand decisions a second. <code>gateway.py</code> becomes Front Door and APIM so bots and unauthenticated callers never reach Python. The in-memory feature store becomes Redis because a feature lookup has to finish in a millisecond or two. <code>catalog.yaml</code> and the identity dict become Cosmos DB so SKU economics, the customer graph, and the offer ledger survive a replica restart. <code>decisions.jsonl</code> becomes Event Hubs with Kafka and a schema registry so every decision is logged with a propensity. Local lake files become ADLS Gen2 Delta tables for point-in-time training and OPE. The numpy jobs under <code>offline/</code> become Azure ML, with Spark in Fabric or Databricks when the joins no longer fit one node. <code>models.json</code> becomes the Azure ML registry, with the same approval gate. <code>control_plane.yaml</code> becomes App Configuration so a kill switch does not wait for a new image. SECTIONS["fallback"] = r'''<section class="card" id="fallback">
  <p class="phase">Failure</p>
  <h2>20. Azure fallbacks (same ladder as the lab)</h2>
  <p>Checkout still needs a price when a dependency is sick, so the ladder is the same one you already coded, just aimed at Azure names. If Redis is down, serve a segment-level default feature vector, mark the call degraded, and still return a price. If Cosmos is down, use the catalog warmed into replica memory at boot; if that is cold, fall back to a static list price. If the causal model times out, reuse last scores in Redis, or the rule-based ladder. If Event Hubs is down, write the local buffer (or a blob) and switch to exploit only so you do not explore into a log you cannot keep. If App Configuration cannot be read, fail closed when the last known flag was kill, otherwise use cached flags no older than a minute. If APIM or Front Door is unhealthy, origin probes fail over to a second Container Apps environment in Canada East in production.</p>
  <label class="step"><input type="checkbox" data-k="p20-fallback" /><span>Chaos: stop Redis in dev. <code>/v1/price</code> still 200 with a price and <code>degraded</code> on the explain endpoint.</span></label>
</section>'''

SECTIONS["done"] = r'''<section class="card" id="done">
  <p class="phase">Done when</p>
  <h2>21. Definition of done</h2>
  <p>You have implemented this project on Azure when a channel can <code>POST /v1/price</code> in Canada Central under a 100 ms p99 and receive only client fields, with no propensity on the wire; when every decision is in Event Hubs with propensity and version pins, and outcomes join within seven days; when kill switch, sticky TTL, and offer redeem work without a redeploy; when nightly OPE can block a bad model and a canary revision can roll back in one command; and when holdout traffic still exists so you can estimate causal effects, not only bandit regret.</p>
  <label class="step"><input type="checkbox" data-k="done-1" /><span>A channel can <code>POST /v1/price</code> in Canada Central, p99 &lt; 100 ms, and get only client fields (no propensity).</span></label>
  <label class="step"><input type="checkbox" data-k="done-2" /><span>Every decision is in Event Hubs with propensity + version pins; outcomes join within 7 days.</span></label>
  <label class="step"><input type="checkbox" data-k="done-3" /><span>Kill switch, sticky TTL, and offer redeem work without a redeploy.</span></label>
  <label class="step"><input type="checkbox" data-k="done-4" /><span>Nightly OPE can block a bad model; canary revisions can roll back in one command.</span></label>
  <label class="step"><input type="checkbox" data-k="done-5" /><span>Holdout traffic still exists so you can estimate causal effects, not only bandit regret.</span></label>
  <p>Start today with login, Docker, and Container Apps. Everything after that is swapping adapters. The pricing brain you already built stays the same. The files that support the first deploy are <code>Dockerfile</code>, <code>.dockerignore</code>, <code>infra/azure-up.ps1</code>, and this HTML runbook.</p>
</section>'''


def replace_section(html: str, sid: str, new: str) -> str:
    marker = f'<section class="card" id="{sid}">'
    start = html.find(marker)
    if start < 0:
        raise SystemExit(f"missing start {sid}")
    nxt = html.find('<section class="card"', start + 1)
    if nxt < 0:
        end = html.find("</article>")
    else:
        end = nxt
    return html[:start] + new.strip() + "\n\n" + html[end:]


html_path = Path("docs/azure-implementation.html")
html = html_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
for sid, body in SECTIONS.items():
    html = replace_section(html, sid, body)

# Soften the header subtitle and the components nav tagline stays in yaml
html = html.replace(
    "Canada Central · follow every checkbox · this file is the runbook",
    "Canada Central · a readable runbook, with commands where you need them",
)

html_path.write_text(html, encoding="utf-8")
print("replaced", list(SECTIONS))

===== FILE: src/pricing_decision/api/app.py =====
from __future__ import annotations

from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

from fastapi import Body, FastAPI, HTTPException, Request
from fastapi.responses import FileResponse, JSONResponse

from pricing_decision import __version__
from pricing_decision.core.exceptions import PricingError
from pricing_decision.core.metrics import metrics
from pricing_decision.architecture import architecture_tabs, azure_components, azure_tabs, project_tabs, science_tabs
from pricing_decision.offline.pipeline import OfflinePipeline, offline_stage_catalog
from pricing_decision.orchestrator import PricingOrchestrator
from pricing_decision.platform import architecture_view, lookup_decision, monitor_snapshot, run_use_case
from pricing_decision.playground import StagePlayground, stage_catalog
from pricing_decision.services.outcomes import OutcomeService

WEB_DIR = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "web"
REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3]


def create_app(orchestrator: PricingOrchestrator | None = None) -> FastAPI:
    app = FastAPI(title="Pricing Decision Service", version=__version__)
    orch = orchestrator or PricingOrchestrator()
    playground = StagePlayground(orch)
    offline = OfflinePipeline(orch)
    outcomes = OutcomeService(offline.lake)
    app.state.orchestrator = orch
    app.state.playground = playground
    app.state.offline = offline
    app.state.outcomes = outcomes

    @app.get("/")
    def home() -> FileResponse:
        return FileResponse(WEB_DIR / "index.html")

    @app.get("/azure")
    def azure_runbook() -> FileResponse:
        return FileResponse(REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "azure-implementation.html")

    @app.get("/project")
    def project_map() -> FileResponse:
        """Folder-and-file map for the lab Project tab."""
        return FileResponse(REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "project-map.html")

    @app.get("/v1/azure/stages")
    def azure_stages() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"stages": azure_tabs()}

    @app.get("/v1/project/stages")
    def project_stages() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"stages": project_tabs()}

    @app.get("/science")
    def science_map() -> FileResponse:
        """Job-description science map: causal, bandits, OPE, constraints."""
        return FileResponse(REPO_ROOT / "docs" / "science.html")

    @app.get("/v1/science/stages")
    def science_stages() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"stages": science_tabs()}

    @app.get("/v1/azure/components")
    def azure_component_catalog() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return azure_components()

    @app.get("/health")
    def health() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"status": "ok", "version": __version__, "pins": orch.cache.snapshot()}

    @app.get("/metrics")
    def metrics_snapshot() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return metrics.snapshot()

    @app.get("/v1/catalog")
    def catalog() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return orch.catalog_view()

    @app.get("/v1/price-board")
    def price_board(channel: str = "web", device: str = "mobile") -> dict[str, Any]:
        return orch.price_board(channel=channel, device=device)

    @app.get("/v1/stages")
    def stages() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {"stages": stage_catalog(), **orch.catalog_view()}

    @app.post("/v1/stages/run")
    def run_stage(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        stage = str(payload.get("stage") or "response")
        request = payload.get("request") or {}
        overrides = payload.get("overrides") or {}
        return playground.run(stage=stage, request=request, overrides=overrides)

    @app.post("/v1/stages/reload")
    def reload_stage_cache() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return playground.reload_cache()

    @app.get("/v1/offline/stages")
    def offline_stages() -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Offline learning lab: stage docs plus current lake snapshot."""
        return {"stages": offline_stage_catalog(), "overview": offline.overview()}

    @app.post("/v1/offline/run")
    def run_offline(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        stage = str(payload.get("stage") or "ol_overview")
        overrides = payload.get("overrides") or {}
        return offline.run(stage, overrides)

    @app.get("/v1/architecture")
    def architecture() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {**architecture_view(), "stages": architecture_tabs()}

    @app.post("/v1/use-cases/{use_case_id}")
    def use_case(use_case_id: str, payload: dict[str, Any] = Body(default_factory=dict)) -> dict[str, Any]:
        result = run_use_case(orch, use_case_id, payload or {})
        if not result.get("ok"):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=result)
        return result

    @app.post("/v1/outcomes")
    def record_outcome(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        result = outcomes.record(payload)
        if not result.get("ok"):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=result)
        return result

    @app.get("/v1/decisions/{decision_id}")
    def get_decision(decision_id: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        result = lookup_decision(orch, offline, decision_id)
        if not result.get("ok"):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail=result)
        return result

    @app.get("/v1/monitor")
    def monitor() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return monitor_snapshot(orch, offline)

    @app.get("/v1/control")
    def get_control() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return orch.control.snapshot()

    @app.post("/v1/control")
    def set_control(payload: dict[str, Any] = Body(default_factory=dict)) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return orch.control.update(payload or {})

    @app.post("/v1/price:batch")
    def price_batch(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        requests = payload.get("requests") or []
        if not isinstance(requests, list) or not requests:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail={"reason": "empty_batch"})
        try:
            decisions = orch.decide_batch(requests)
        except PricingError as exc:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=exc.status_code, detail={"reason": exc.reason, "message": exc.message})
        return {
            "n": len(decisions),
            "responses": [d.response.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True) for d in decisions],
        }

    @app.get("/v1/offers/{code}")
    def get_offer(code: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        rec = orch.coupons.lookup(code)
        if not rec:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=404, detail={"reason": "unknown_offer"})
        return {"ok": True, "offer": rec}

    @app.post("/v1/offers/{code}/redeem")
    def redeem_offer(code: str) -> dict[str, Any]:
        result = orch.coupons.redeem(code)
        if not result.get("ok"):
            raise HTTPException(status_code=400, detail=result)
        return result

    @app.post("/v1/price")
    def price(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        try:
            decision = orch.decide(payload)
        except PricingError as exc:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=exc.status_code, detail={"reason": exc.reason, "message": exc.message})
        body = decision.response.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True)
        return body

    @app.post("/v1/price:explain")
    def price_explain(payload: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
        """Internal debug endpoint — not for clients."""
        try:
            decision = orch.decide(payload)
        except PricingError as exc:
            raise HTTPException(status_code=exc.status_code, detail={"reason": exc.reason, "message": exc.message})
        return {
            "response": decision.response.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True),
            "experience": decision.experience,
            "degraded": decision.context.degraded,
            "degraded_reasons": decision.context.degraded_reasons,
            "arms": [a.model_dump() for a in decision.context.arms],
            "scores": [s.model_dump() for s in decision.context.scores],
            "bandit": decision.context.bandit.model_dump() if decision.context.bandit else None,
            "timings_ms": decision.context.stage_timings_ms,
        }

    @app.post("/v1/admin/reload")
    def reload_models() -> dict[str, Any]:
        return orch.cache.hot_reload()

    @app.exception_handler(Exception)
    async def unhandled(_: Request, exc: Exception) -> JSONResponse:
        return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={"reason": "internal_error", "message": str(exc)})

    return app


app = create_app()

def system_stage() -> dict[str, Any]:
    arch = load_yaml("architecture.yaml")
    if not isinstance(arch, dict):
        arch = {}
    loops = arch.get("loops") or {}

    def pack(title: str, key: str) -> dict[str, str]:
        steps = loops.get(key) or []
        detail = " ".join(f"{i + 1}) {step}" for i, step in enumerate(steps))
        return {"title": title, "detail": detail}

    return {
        "id": "system",
        "number": None,
        "title": arch.get("title", "Full architecture"),
        "tagline": arch.get("tagline", ""),
        "about": arch.get("about", ""),
        "in_short": arch.get("in_short", ""),
        "try": arch.get("try", ""),
        "process": [
            pack("Online PDS — the hot path", "online"),
            pack("Offline learning — the night shift", "offline"),
            pack("Feedback loop — how models get back to checkout", "feedback"),
        ],
        "loops": loops,
    }

===== FILE: src/pricing_decision/cli.py =====
from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import sys

from pricing_decision.orchestrator import PricingOrchestrator


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Pricing Decision Service")
    sub = parser.add_subparsers(dest="cmd", required=True)

    decide = sub.add_parser("decide", help="Run one pricing decision from JSON")
    decide.add_argument("--file", "-f", help="Path to request JSON. Reads stdin if omitted.")
    decide.add_argument("--explain", action="store_true", help="Print internal scores and arms")

    sub.add_parser("serve", help="Run the FastAPI server")

    args = parser.parse_args(argv)
    if args.cmd == "serve":
        import uvicorn

        from pricing_decision.config import get_settings

        settings = get_settings()
        uvicorn.run("pricing_decision.api.app:app", host=settings.host, port=settings.port, reload=False)
        return 0

    if args.file:
        with open(args.file, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
            payload = json.load(fh)
    else:
        payload = json.load(sys.stdin)

    orch = PricingOrchestrator()
    decision = orch.decide(payload)
    if args.explain:
        print(
            json.dumps(
                {
                    "response": decision.response.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True),
                    "arms": [a.model_dump() for a in decision.context.arms],
                    "scores": [s.model_dump() for s in decision.context.scores],
                    "bandit": decision.context.bandit.model_dump() if decision.context.bandit else None,
                    "experience": decision.experience,
                    "timings_ms": decision.context.stage_timings_ms,
                },
                indent=2,
                default=str,
            )
        )
    else:
        print(json.dumps(decision.response.model_dump(mode="json", exclude_none=True), indent=2, default=str))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())


===== FILE: src/pricing_decision/config.py =====
from __future__ import annotations

from functools import lru_cache
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import yaml
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from pydantic_settings import BaseSettings, SettingsConfigDict


ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
CONFIG_DIR = ROOT / "configs"


def load_yaml(name: str) -> Any:
    path = CONFIG_DIR / name
    with path.open("r", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return yaml.safe_load(fh) or {}


class Settings(BaseSettings):
    model_config = SettingsConfigDict(env_prefix="PDS_", extra="ignore")

    env: str = "local"
    host: str = "0.0.0.0"
    port: int = 8080
    log_buffer_dir: Path = ROOT / "data" / "log_buffer"
    kafka_enabled: bool = False
    kafka_topic: str = "pricing.decisions.v1"
    offer_ttl_seconds: int = 600
    epsilon: float = 0.05
    propensity_mc_samples: int = 256
    propensity_floor: float = 0.05
    charm_pricing: bool = True
    default_currency: str = "USD"
    unknown_sku_policy: str = "error"  # error | category_fallback
    latency_budget_ms: int = 69


class VersionPinsConfig(BaseModel):
    policy_id: str
    causal_model_id: str
    guardrail_version: str
    candidate_set_version: str
    bandit_version: str
    reward_definition: str = "margin"
    response_schema_version: str = "v1"


class RuntimeConfig(BaseModel):
    settings: Settings
    versions: VersionPinsConfig
    ladders: dict[str, Any]
    guardrails: dict[str, Any]
    features: dict[str, Any]
    catalog: dict[str, Any]


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_settings() -> Settings:
    return Settings()


@lru_cache(maxsize=1)
def get_runtime_config() -> RuntimeConfig:
    return RuntimeConfig(
        settings=get_settings(),
        versions=VersionPinsConfig.model_validate(load_yaml("versions.yaml")),
        ladders=load_yaml("ladders.yaml"),
        guardrails=load_yaml("guardrails.yaml"),
        features=load_yaml("features.yaml"),
        catalog=load_yaml("catalog.yaml"),
    )


def reload_runtime_config() -> RuntimeConfig:
    get_runtime_config.cache_clear()
    get_settings.cache_clear()
    return get_runtime_config()

===== FILE: src/pricing_decision/core/exceptions.py =====
class PricingError(Exception):
    """Base error for the pricing decision service."""

    def __init__(self, message: str, *, reason: str = "error", status_code: int = 500):
        super().__init__(message)
        self.message = message
        self.reason = reason
        self.status_code = status_code


class ValidationFailedError(PricingError):
    def __init__(self, message: str, *, reason: str = "validation_error"):
        super().__init__(message, reason=reason, status_code=400)


class SkuNotFoundError(PricingError):
    def __init__(self, sku: str):
        super().__init__(f"Unknown SKU: {sku}", reason="unknown_sku", status_code=404)
        self.sku = sku


class FallbackError(PricingError):
    """Raised inside a stage so the orchestrator can degrade, not abort."""

    def __init__(self, message: str, *, reason: str, stage: str):
        super().__init__(message, reason=reason, status_code=200)
        self.stage = stage


===== FILE: src/pricing_decision/core/ids.py =====
from __future__ import annotations

import os
import time
import uuid
from datetime import datetime, timezone


def utc_now() -> datetime:
    return datetime.now(timezone.utc)


def uuid7() -> str:
    """Time-ordered UUID (RFC 9562 style) without requiring Python 3.13."""
    if hasattr(uuid, "uuid7"):
        return str(uuid.uuid7())

    unix_ts_ms = int(time.time() * 1000)
    rand = int.from_bytes(os.urandom(10), "big")
    time_hi = unix_ts_ms & 0xFFFFFFFFFFFF
    uuid_int = (time_hi << 80) | (0x7 << 76) | ((rand >> 62) << 64) | (0b10 << 62) | (rand & ((1 << 62) - 1))
    return str(uuid.UUID(int=uuid_int))


def new_trace_ids() -> tuple[str, str]:
    return uuid.uuid4().hex, uuid.uuid4().hex[:16]


===== FILE: src/pricing_decision/core/metrics.py =====
from __future__ import annotations

from collections import defaultdict
from threading import Lock
from typing import Any


class MetricsRegistry:
    """Lightweight in-process counters/histograms. Prometheus is optional."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._lock = Lock()
        self.counters: dict[str, float] = defaultdict(float)
        self.histograms: dict[str, list[float]] = defaultdict(list)

    def inc(self, name: str, labels: dict[str, Any] | None = None, value: float = 1.0) -> None:
        key = self._key(name, labels)
        with self._lock:
            self.counters[key] += value

    def observe(self, name: str, value: float, labels: dict[str, Any] | None = None) -> None:
        key = self._key(name, labels)
        with self._lock:
            self.histograms[key].append(value)

    def snapshot(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        with self._lock:
            return {
                "counters": dict(self.counters),
                "histograms": {k: self._summary(v) for k, v in self.histograms.items()},
            }

    @staticmethod
    def _key(name: str, labels: dict[str, Any] | None) -> str:
        if not labels:
            return name
        parts = ",".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in sorted(labels.items()))
        return f"{name}{{{parts}}}"

    @staticmethod
    def _summary(values: list[float]) -> dict[str, float]:
        if not values:
            return {"count": 0, "avg": 0.0}
        ordered = sorted(values)
        n = len(ordered)
        p99_idx = min(n - 1, int(n * 0.99))
        return {
            "count": n,
            "avg": sum(ordered) / n,
            "p50": ordered[n // 2],
            "p99": ordered[p99_idx],
        }


metrics = MetricsRegistry()

        self.degraded = True
        if reason not in self.degraded_reasons:
            self.degraded_reasons.append(reason)

        return {s.arm_id: s for s in self.scores}

===== FILE: src/pricing_decision/core/tracing.py =====
from __future__ import annotations

import logging
import time
from contextlib import contextmanager
from typing import Iterator

from pricing_decision.core.metrics import metrics
from pricing_decision.core.models import DecisionContext

logger = logging.getLogger("pds")


@contextmanager
def stage_span(ctx: DecisionContext, stage: str) -> Iterator[None]:
    start = time.perf_counter()
    logger.info(
        "stage_start",
        extra={"decision_id": ctx.decision_id, "trace_id": ctx.trace_id, "stage": stage},
    )
    try:
        yield
    finally:
        elapsed_ms = (time.perf_counter() - start) * 1000
        ctx.stage_timings_ms[stage] = round(elapsed_ms, 3)
        metrics.observe(f"pds_{stage}_latency_ms", elapsed_ms)
        logger.info(
            "stage_end",
            extra={
                "decision_id": ctx.decision_id,
                "trace_id": ctx.trace_id,
                "stage": stage,
                "latency_ms": round(elapsed_ms, 3),
            },
        )
